newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian 1996 trade gap up 13.9 pct to $3.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Croatian 1996 trade gap up 13.9 pct to $3.3 bln.

text.p: Croatian trade deficit rose 13.9 percent to a record $3.28 billion in 1996, due to a steep rise in consumer goods imports and fall in the exports of production materials.
The State Bureau of Statistics' data showed imports reaching $7.79 billion in 1996, or 3.7 percent up from the previous year. Exports at the same time fell 2.6 percent to $4.51 billion.
The sharpest drop of 8.5 percent was recorded in the exports of production materials, which account for more than half of the country's total trade deficit.
The imporst of consumers goods rose 5.5 percent to $2.15 billion, while imports of production materials fell 0.7 percent to $4.12 billion.
Both imports and exports of investment goods rose at the sharpest rates of 14.9 and 28.6 percent respectively.
Croatian exports to the European Union countries fell 13.8 percent to $2.3 billion in 1996, while imports fell 0.8 percent to $4.63 billion.

Of the former Yugoslav republics, Croatia had a trade surplus of $485,139 with the neighbouring Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1996, despite a 628-percent rise in imports from the war-ravaged country. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4551840
